episode_title: EP 283 Retreat Audit: Why Your Retreat Isn't Filling (A Real-Life Case Study)
question: What are the most common landing page mistakes that prevent retreat registrations from converting?
transcript_excerpt: The number one issue is not being able to clearly communicate who the retreat is for and what is actually happening. Many retreat leaders use flowery language that appeals emotionally but fails to communicate to AI and SEO systems. Within three to four seconds, visitors should immediately understand if the retreat is for them, what problem it solves, and how it will be transformed. The landing page must clearly answer: who exactly is this for, what problem are you solving, what is the transformation or promise, why you, why this retreat, and why now.

episode_title: EP 283 Retreat Audit: Why Your Retreat Isn't Filling (A Real-Life Case Study)
question: How frequently should retreat leaders engage in marketing and content creation to fill their retreats?
transcript_excerpt: If you are going to host a retreat and you cannot spend at least 30 minutes every working day working on your retreat at minimum, you probably should not host a retreat. During that 30 minutes you should do one social post, one story post, reach out via email, get into groups and chat about your retreat, or create connections with others. With AI, an incredible amount of work can be accomplished in 30 minutes, and even better in an hour.

episode_title: EP 283 Retreat Audit: Why Your Retreat Isn't Filling (A Real-Life Case Study)
question: What is the impact of organic social media reach and audience visibility for retreat marketing?
transcript_excerpt: Less than 1% of your audience sees your stuff anyway. With the way attention spans work and the amount of information people consume digitally, people have to see things 17 to 20 times before it actually hits the part of the brain that goes, hey, this might be for me. As soon as you are sick of yourself talking about it, you are barely scratching the surface.

episode_title: EP 283 Retreat Audit: Why Your Retreat Isn't Filling (A Real-Life Case Study)
question: Why should retreat leaders prioritize keyword strategy over hashtags for content optimization?
transcript_excerpt: Hashtags are dead. Algorithms scan the content and ignore or sometimes penalize things that have hashtags. What algorithms want to see instead is that your content is optimized with the actual words and keywords you are using. Your content has to have your keywords already built into it. Keyword strategy matters in blogs, posts, landing pages, emails, everything.

episode_title: EP 283 Retreat Audit: Why Your Retreat Isn't Filling (A Real-Life Case Study)
question: How should retreat leaders structure calls-to-action on landing pages to maximize bookings?
transcript_excerpt: If there are too many options like book your spot, book a call, or join this list with three, four, or five different CTAs, it creates friction. One clear call-to-action throughout the whole landing page is preferred, such as reserve your spot or grab your spot. Maybe somewhere at the bottom for those not ready yet, offer book a call, but the primary focus should be one main action.

episode_title: EP 283 Retreat Audit: Why Your Retreat Isn't Filling (A Real-Life Case Study)
question: What lead time should retreat leaders allow between booking announcement and event date?
transcript_excerpt: This is tricky because it depends on your audience, your retreat, and many different factors. More often than not, six to 12 months is preferred because visibility compounds over that time. People make buying decisions differently now, and many book things that are further in the future so they can spread out payments or allow for planning purposes, vacation, work, and kids.

episode_title: EP 283 Retreat Audit: Why Your Retreat Isn't Filling (A Real-Life Case Study)
question: What credibility elements should retreat leaders include to build trust with potential guests?
transcript_excerpt: Testimonials, video ones, photos, reviews, media, podcast appearances, and your about page need to be super clear and abundant. If you are new in this business, have worked with somebody in some capacity and get those testimonials ready. Make sure your bio is super clear. Avoid AI pictures and AI videos because people can tell and it does not feel authentic. The ugly videos, everyday videos, real videos, and authentic videos are what is actually doing really well now in social media.

episode_title: EP 283 Retreat Audit: Why Your Retreat Isn't Filling (A Real-Life Case Study)
question: How should retreat leaders use email marketing to support their retreat business?
transcript_excerpt: Email is still the most powerful way to do business and it is the list you own. It is a great trust builder. Even if you only have 10 people on your email list, you should be using it. At minimum do one email every other week. Some people do it every day, which is not everyone's jam, but every other week is minimum.

episode_title: EP 283 Retreat Audit: Why Your Retreat Isn't Filling (A Real-Life Case Study)
question: What role should FAQ sections play on retreat landing pages?
transcript_excerpt: An FAQ section is a huge driver for AI. You should absolutely 100% put an FAQ section on your website and use the same kind of questions that people actually ask about your retreat. Ask the actual questions that your guest would type into AI and make it an FAQ. This is also done on all blogs and is a huge driver for search and AI understanding.

episode_title: EP 283 Retreat Audit: Why Your Retreat Isn't Filling (A Real-Life Case Study)
question: Should retreat leaders focus marketing messaging on features like yoga classes and meals or on transformation benefits?
transcript_excerpt: No one is buying the yoga classes or the organic meals. They are buying peace, confidence, connection, healing, belonging, growth, and learning. Features are secondary. Make sure transformation and benefits are the focus, not the stuff.
